Subject: Non-standard private deployments — exception + resource ask (MedPath Diagnostics)

Team,

Quick context: MedPath Diagnostics (deal MP-2026-124) is pushing for a VPC-first private deployment with an optional air-gapped on-prem appliance for a subset of sites. They provided a security matrix (attached) and a draft LOA. Procurement wants a clear feasibility summary, product ask list, and a suggested resourcing commitment so they can sign a PO by end of Q3.

Key asks from them:
- Private control plane in their VPC with customer-managed KMS (must-have)
- On-prem appliance image + support for disconnected updates for 2 high-security sites (optional but likely)
- Audit logs with 2-year retention and per-token tracing for compliance

What I need from this thread: a short (1) tech feasibility note from infra, (2) product impact and roadmap ask, and (3) a suggested staff/PM/eng commitments (FTEs + calendar runway) that we can include in an exception request to Legal/Compliance.

Attachments: medpath_security_matrix.pdf, mp_mop_loa_draft.docx

Proposed next step: 30-min sync with MedPath (technical + procurement) — they suggested week of 6/15. Can infra + product give initial write-ups by EOD 6/11? I can coordinate the meeting.

Thanks,
Neha

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Non-standard private deployments — exception + resource ask (MedPath Diagnostics)

Neha — thanks for the summary. High-level feasibility notes below; detailed runbook to follow if you want it.

1) VPC private control plane (customer VPC):
- Technically feasible but this is a non-trivial product surface: we need a lightweight control-plane agent that runs in their VPC to handle registration, heartbeat, and secure bootstrap.
- KMS integration: OK via external KMS APIs (AWS KMS/Azure KeyVault/GCP KMS). We'll need short-lived certs + mTLS for control-plane RPCs.
- Networking: requires dedicated NAT/Gateway config + peering or PrivateLink depending on customer cloud. Expect ~2 dedicated infra engineer-weeks to build the initial hardened agent + networking templates.

2) On-prem air-gapped appliance (optional):
- We'll provide an appliance image (container runtime + runtime supervisor). Disconnected updates are the hard part: we must support offline package bundles and a verified update signer.
- Compliance ask: runbook for installation + rollback support. Estimate: 4-6 eng-weeks to create build/release pipeline + signed update process, plus 2 weeks of SRE validation per customer site.

3) Observability & audit logs:
- Per-token tracing with 2-year retention implies storage and indexing costs; we can store logs in customer-controlled S3 buckets if they want data residency, otherwise we absorb storage (cost impact).
- We should scope retention SLAs and export tooling. Estimate: product + infra collaboration 2-3 sprints for base functionality.

Open questions for MedPath (we should confirm before committing):
- Which cloud(s) are in scope? (AWS-only reduces complexity)
- Expected TPS and peak concurrency per site (KV / token loads)
- Who will manage the appliance hardware (customer-managed onsite)?

I'll draft a short feasibility memo (1-2 pages) and costed resource estimate by EOD 6/11 as requested. If Product prefers a different priority, let me know.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Director, Platform Infra
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Thanks — useful. A few product-facing notes / roadmap impact items: 

Product asks (must-haves to include in feasibility):
- Customer-managed control plane mode (API + agent) — needs a small surface in our API to toggle pinning and KMS delegation.
- Per-tenant audit logs export (s3/gcs) with schema versioning and tooling to rehydrate for debug.
- Secure update mechanism for appliance images (signed releases + replay protection).
- Admin console features for tenant admins: role-based access + audit search.

Roadmap implications:
- To deliver minimal viable private VPC (customer VPC + KMS) we should allocate 1 PM (0.2 FTE) + 2 infra engineers + 1 platform eng (3 months runway) to avoid blocking Hosted roadmap.
- For the on-prem appliance path, it's a separate stream: 1 PM (0.2 FTE) + 2 engs + 1 SRE for validation (approx 2 months after initial VPC work).
- If we accept this as an exception for MedPath, we should require a paid onboarding engineering block (professional services) to cover site validation and any design customizations.

Compliance / Legal asks to surface now:
- We'll need SOC2 evidence, penetration-test artifacts, and export controls sign-off for appliance images. Hannah, can you advise on the list we should provide?

I'll attach a short note on the roadmap impact (roadmap_impact_notes.md) for the exec/finance review.

—Laura Bennett | Product Lead, Private Deployments
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Folks — one commercial note before we finalize resourcing asks: MedPath is an enterprise prospect with multi-year potential, but they have procurement constraints and will push hard on credits and onboarding discounts. My recommendation: we treat the VPC control-plane work as a billable engineering engagement (fixed-price onboarding) and include a discount tied to an annual committed usage (dedicated reserved capacity).

Also: if Product/Infra expects >3 months to deliver critical compliance items, we should be explicit that Legal will require an Exception Form with an acceptance of residual risk and a stronger SLA. I'll loop Legal if we decide to proceed; can someone prepare the business case (value vs. risk) and an estimated discount model?

I can own negotiation with Procurement once we have the tech + cost note. For the meeting week of 6/15, propose Tue 6/16 10:00 AM PT. Amir from MedPath said he can do Tue/Wed morning.

—Vivek
